observations:
Torah #271 is a brief three-sentence teaching about the reciprocal relationship between holy boldness (עַזּוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה), speaking openly with one's teacher (דִּבּוּר עִם הָרַב), and intensified divine service (עֲבוֹדַת ה'). The Rebbe's point is precisely that these three things form a mutually reinforcing causal loop — each causes the next, which causes the first again — and that one cannot identify the starting point. This is a teaching about circular eitza causation, not about shared essence (bechina).

The criteria for proposing a new package requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. Torah #271 fails this test on two grounds:
1. LANGUAGE: The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the source text. There is no bechina language.
2. STRUCTURE: Every connection in the text is a 'מֵחֲמַת' (because of) or 'עַל יְדֵי' (through) construction — these are unambiguously causal relationships.

Even if one were to consider whether any concepts in this Torah share a common essence that could justify a package, the three main concepts (עַזּוּת, דִּבּוּר, עֲבוֹדָה) are fundamentally distinct phenomena: boldness is a character trait, speaking is an action, divine service is a practice. They do not share the same essential nature — they cause each other. This is precisely the distinction the framework defines: 'does one produce the other, or are they both expressions of the same thing?' Here, one clearly produces the other.

Conclusion: Torah #271 is a pure eitza teaching. No bechina packages are possible or appropriate for this Torah.
